title: Did you know… Ananias was afraid to obey when sent to Paul?
paragraphs: Did you know… Ananias was afraid to obey when sent to Paul?

He knew the voice.
But fear still spoke louder.
Yes—Acts of the Apostles 9 tells it raw: when God called Ananias of Damascus to go to Paul the Apostle, he hesitated.
“Lord… I’ve heard about this man.”

Translation?
He’s dangerous.
He hurts people like me.
Pause there.

Ananias wasn’t rebellious.
He was honest.
He knew Saul’s reputation—persecutor, destroyer, hunter of believers. The kind of name that makes your chest tighten.

And God said:
“Go.”

No long explanation.
No safety guarantee.
Just purpose.
But here’s what we miss…

God didn’t rebuke Ananias for feeling fear.
He reframed his vision.
“Go, for he is a chosen instrument of Mine.”

Chosen.
Not because Saul was clean—
but because grace was coming for him.
And that’s where everything flips.

The man Ananias feared…
became the man who would preach Christ to nations.

The threat…
became the testimony.
Listen—this is Gospel ground:

Jesus doesn’t just save the safe.
He redeems the worst stories and turns them into weapons of grace.

Ananias walked into a room with fear in his bones…
and called a former killer,
“Brother.”

That’s not human courage.
That’s Christ at work.

Because at the center of this story is not Ananias’ bravery—
it’s Jesus transforming Saul.

Sin → Confronted
Heart → Broken
Life → Rewritten

And the same Jesus who stopped Saul on that road
is still stopping people today.
Maybe even you.

So if God is asking you to step toward something scary—
a person, a calling, a conversation—
don’t wait for fear to disappear.
Walk anyway.

Because on the other side of your obedience
might be someone’s redemption story.

And maybe…
God is also rewriting your name in the process.
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
